activity_context.topic_title: Integration by Substitution With Inverse Hyperbolic Functions

feedback.worked_solution:
Let's rewrite our integral as

$$
\int \frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}-8}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{8}}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{{(\frac{x}{\sqrt{8}})}^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{{(\frac{x}{2\sqrt{2}})}^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

This integral resembles the basic integral for the inverse hyperbolic cosine,

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{{u}^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}u=\operatorname{arcosh}⁡u+C.
$$

The only difference is that instead of ${u}^{2}$ as the variable, we have ${(\frac{x}{2\sqrt{2}})}^{2}.$

So, let's substitute $u=\frac{x}{2\sqrt{2}}.$ Differentiating, we get 

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\,⟹\,\text{d}x=2\sqrt{2}\,\text{d}u.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate it, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}-8}}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{{(\frac{x}{2\sqrt{2}})}^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{{u}^{2}-1}}\cdot 2\sqrt{2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\sqrt{2}\int \frac{\text{d}u}{\sqrt{{u}^{2}-1}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\operatorname{arcosh}⁡u+C \\  & =\sqrt{2}\operatorname{arcosh}⁡(\frac{x}{2\sqrt{2}})+C\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
